prs.author: Genmin

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects any request whose Accept header doesn't list both application/json and text/event-stream, even though JSON response mode only ever returns application/json — clients sending Accept: application/json alone get a spurious 406. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same Accept-header validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts and ship functionally identical changesets. #1996 replaces the check with a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that splits the header into media-range entries, trims/lowercases them, honors q=0 exclusion, and matches wildcard type/subtype per RFC 7231 semantics. #2046's visible diff instead computes acceptsJson via a plain substring `.includes('application/json')` check on the raw header, which won't correctly exclude an explicitly disallowed `application/json;q=0` entry or handle wildcard Accept values (`*/*`, `application/*`) the way #1996's parser does.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: buildWellKnownPath() only stripped a single trailing slash from the pathname before appending '/.well-known/...', so paths with multiple trailing slashes (or edge cases around the root path) produced malformed discovery URLs like '/foo//.well-known/oauth-authorization-server'. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs replace the same single-slash '.slice(0,-1)' logic in buildWellKnownPath with the identical global regex fix (pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '')), so they touch the exact same lines and would conflict if both merged. #2215 goes further: it factors the normalization into a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper and updates shouldAttemptFallback's root check from `pathname === '/'` to `pathname === ''` to match the new convention where the root path normalizes to an empty string. #2214 changes buildWellKnownPath the same way but does not update shouldAttemptFallback, leaving the root-path comparison out of sync with the new normalization and the redundant-fallback-at-root bug unaddressed.
